title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development.

title: Gut microbiome patterns in a multi-ethnic Asian population within a shared urban environment.
abstract: The gut microbiome composition varies across human populations, but its characteristics and determinants in a multi-ethnic setting remain incompletely understood. Singapore, a multicultural city-state, provides a context in which culturally diverse groups share a broadly similar built environment. Using the Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) cohort, we profiled the gut microbiome of ethnic Chinese, Indian, and Malay participants (n = 861) residing in the country. These ethnicity-diet-microbio

title: Gut Holdemania filiformis raises brain isoallopregnanolone in progesterone-treated female mice.
abstract: Neuroactive 5α-steroids modulate γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor signaling and are of growing therapeutic interest: allopregnanolone (3α,5α) is a positive allosteric modulator, whereas its 3β-epimer isoallopregnanolone antagonizes this action and is itself in clinical development. Their formation has been attributed to host enzymes in the liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, whereas a contribution from any individual gut bacterium has not been demonstrated. title: The gut microbiome is associated with structural and functional brain alterations in adolescents with social anxiety disorder.
abstract: Social anxiety disorder (SAD) commonly emerges in childhood or early adolescence and is associated with persistent impairments in social and emotional functioning. Although structural and functional brain abnormalities have been reported in SAD, the potential involvement of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in adolescent SAD remains poorly understood.

title: Acetate-FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are requir
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Gut microbiota-driven imbalance of the gut-brain-immune homeostatic network in constipation: Pathogenic mechanisms and evolving therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Chronic constipation (CC) is increasingly recognized as a systems-level disorder that cannot be explained by impaired intestinal motility alone. Here, we integrate evidence from clinical cohorts, animal models, and mechanistic studies to examine how gut microbial dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites perturb epithelial barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, enteric neural activity, and gut-brain signaling. We propose a "gut-brain-immune homeostatic network" in which short-chain fatty acids

title: Disturbances of the gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites as key actors in vagotomy-induced mastitis in mice.
Ovarian function via gut microbiota-driven serotonin dysregulation in zebrafish.
abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is frequently detected in aquatic environments, yet its effects on reproduction through gut microbiota-mediated pathways remain unclear. Adult female zebrafish were exposed to 5,000 ng/L CIP for 30 days and evaluated using histology, hormone assays, metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). CIP impaired folliculogenesis, reduced follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, and estradiol levels, and disrupted intestinal barr

title: Oral live and heat-killed Ligilactobacillus salivarius Ls.0403 alleviate MC903-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation and are associated with gut microbiota changes in mice.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that often requires long-term management. Probiotics have been investigated as adjunctive approaches for AD, but their effects are highly strain specific. Among these, Ligilactobacillus salivarius has shown potential in previous AD studies, yet the effects of different strains remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we screened 19 human-derived L. salivarius isolates and selected Ls.0403, which exhibited favorab

title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice.
abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. The levels of sitosterol sulfate (SIS), campesterol sulfate, and stigmasterol sulfate, the three major phytosterol sulfates, along with copros

title: Multiomic crosstalk between plasma metabolites and inflammation in IBD via MR and mouse validation.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by gut dysbiosis and recurrent intestinal inflammation. Integrating bibliometric analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-platform protein pQTL MR, colocalization, and druggability assessment, we dissected gut microbiota-driven plasma metabolite-inflammation homeostasis axes in IBD. MR and mediation analyses identified multi-omics biomarkers and 24 candidate therapeutic metabolites organiz

title: Gut microbiota composition of India's Baiga tribe: Insights from an indigenous particularly vulnerable tribal group.
abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. To examine this shift within the Indian subcontinent, we used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiota of 50 adults: 25 from the indigenous, foraging, and particularly vulnerable Baiga tribe and 25 from an urban population in Bhopal, Central India. The Baiga maintained a diverse ecosystem enriched with fiber-degrading bacteria such as Roseburia

title: A microbial metabolite reframes the gut-kidney axis in calcium oxalate nephropathy†.
abstract: Kidney stone disease has long been viewed primarily as a disorder of urinary supersaturation, with therapeutic strategies focusing on reducing urinary oxalate and preventing crystal formation. Increasing evidence, however, suggests that renal epithelial injury, immune responses, and the gut microbiota are integral components of disease pathogenesis. In their recent article, published in The Journal of Pathology, Li, Chen, Lin, Jian et al provide compelling evidence that microbiota-derived trypto

title: An HA-Coated Akkermansia-Paeoniflorin Biohybrid Enables Sustained Oral Delivery for Gut-Gonad Axis Protection.
abstract: Living biohybrid materials offer a unique opportunity to couple oral drug delivery with host-microbiome interactions, yet maintaining carrier integrity, cargo retention, and biological function under gastrointestinal constraints remains challenging. Here, we engineered a hyaluronic acid (HA)-coated Akkermansia muciniphila-paeoniflorin biohybrid (PF@AKK@HA) through vacuum-enabled paeoniflorin loading followed by HA shell stabilization. Structural and colloidal analyses confirmed preserved bacteri

title: Distinct Probiotic Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 in a Rat Model of Spleen qi Deficiency Syndrome.
abstract: Spleen qi deficiency syndrome (SDS) is characterized by chronic fatigue, gastrointestinal dysfunction, and systemic metabolic disturbances and has been associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and chronic inflammation. This study evaluated the effects of two probiotic strains, Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 (LFP) and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 (BAP), in an SDS rat model. Both probiotic strains significantly ameliorated SDS-like phenotypes, including reduced bl

title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more

title: Antibiotic heteroresistance observed across commensal Lactobacillus species.
abstract: Lactobacilli are prevalent members of the microbiota in the intestinal and reproductive tracts of humans and other species. They are commonly used in probiotics due to their beneficial effects on human health, including their association with protection from numerous chronic diseases. In addition, these microbes are often prescribed to maintain their presence in the host during antibiotic therapy, as well as to treat diarrhea caused by antibiotics. Despite many studies examining the beneficial e

title: A hydrogen peroxide-tolerant Bifidobacterium longum strain improves colitis by resisting oxidative stress.
abstract: Inflammation-associated oxidative stress can limit the viability and efficacy of obligate anaerobic probiotics such as Bifidobacterium. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by sustained intestinal inflammation accompanied by elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS), creating an unfavorable niche for oxygen-sensitive commensals.

title: EndD mediates butyrate-dependent toxin release and sporulation in Clostridioides difficile.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile is an urgent threat to human health. Current treatments for C. difficile infections (CDIs) are antibiotics and microbiome restoration therapy (MRT) for recurrent cases. However, antibiotics contribute to antibiotic resistance and recurrent CDIs, and the long-term sustainability and accessibility of MRTs remain to be determined. Since a dysbiotic gut microbiome is the primary risk factor for CDI, a better understanding of the interactions between C. difficile, the microbi

title: Population-scale identification of gut commensals that antagonize antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat, yet microbiome-encoded defenses against antibiotic resistance gene (ARG)-associated pathogens remain poorly defined. Here, we analyze 12,238 human gut metagenomes and prioritize 159 commensal species ("coexcluders") that show inverse associations with ARG-associated pathogenic taxa. title: Synergistic Anti-Tumour Strategy Combining Valerate, Butyrate, Neurotensin Pathway Modulation from Gut Microbiota, and Non-Typhoidal Salmonella in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with disease progression and treatment outcomes influenced by tumour heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Increasing evidence highlights the gut-liver axis as an important regulator of hepatic inflammation, metabolic homeostasis, and tumour-associated immune responses. title: Human Milk-Derived Synbiotics Attenuate DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice via Promoting Intestinal Colonization of Lachnospira.
abstract: 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL) exhibits prebiotic properties, but its ability to enhance probiotic efficacy in ulcerative colitis (UC) is incompletely understood. Here, we show that 2'-FL effectively enhances the protective effect of Bifidobacterium bifidum B-67 against DSS-induced colitis in mice. Combination therapy outperformed individual treatments, suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and restoring mucosal integrity. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Commensal Bacteroides Strains Restrict Intestinal Colonization by Multidrug-Resistant Campylobacter jejuni.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Campylobacter jejuni is a foodborne pathogen that threatens public health and food safety. Intestinal colonization is a prerequisite for infection, yet protective commensal bacteria and the potential contributions of microbial metabolites remain poorly defined. This study integrates in vitro co-culture assays, epithelial cell models, mouse infection experiments, and multi-omics analyses to identify protective gut commensals and explore potential mechanisms. Most commens

title: Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving the gut-brain axis, yet genome-resolved characterization of bacterial and viral communities with metabolic context remains limited. Here, we performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling in a high-altitude cohort comprising patients with PD and environmentally matched spouse controls (living at approximately 1,900 m altitude). We reconstructed 455 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and 2,957

title: Food-Grade Kappa-Carrageenan Induces Liver Injury through the FXR/FGF15 Pathway in Mice.
abstract: Food-grade carrageenan (CGN) is widely used as a food additive, but its potential health risks remain controversial. This study investigated the effects of dietary food-grade kappa-CGN (κ-CGN) on liver health in mice. Our findings demonstrated that dietary κ-CGN induced liver inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis. Metabolomic analyses identified elevated circulatory bile acids as a potential contributor to κ-CGN-induced liver injury. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed gut microbiota dysbiosis a
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: The impact of childhood obesity on the developing skeleton.
abstract: Childhood obesity is an increasingly prevalent global health concern associated with significant metabolic, endocrine, and skeletal consequences. During critical periods of growth and peak bone mineralisation, excessive adiposity may impair skeletal development by disrupting bone formation and remodeling. The effects of obesity on bone metabolism are complex and multifactorial, involving altered mechanical loading, hormonal dysregulation, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Key mediators, includ

title: Alcohol-Tolerant Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01 Prevents Acute Alcoholic Liver Injury by Reducing Blood Alcohol Concentration and Modulating Gut Microbiota in Mice.
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health concern with limited effective interventions. This study screened and identified a lactic acid bacterial strain with potent ethanol-degrading capacity, designated as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01. Sequence alignment-based annotation of the L. plantarum LBP-L01 genome identified genes involved in alcohol metabolism. LBP-L01 exhibited robust safety profiles, as demonstrated by its tolerance, adhesive capacity, low biogenic amine produc

title: Conformational and Rheological Changes of Hericium erinaceus Polysaccharides Driven by Molecular Weight Reduction and Their Impact on Prebiotic Effects.
abstract: Hericium erinaceus polysaccharide was degraded using microwave-assisted enzymatic hydrolysis to obtain four gradient molecular weight fractions (HePs). This study investigated the effects of molecular weight on their structural, rheological, and prebiotic properties. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Polysaccharide from Ziyang black tea prevents high-fat diet-induced obesity by remodeling gut microbiota and promoting adipose thermogenesis.
abstract: This study aims to explore the mechanism of obesity prevention by polysaccharide extracted from Ziyang black tea (BTP). BTP is an acidic heteropolysaccharide, mainly composed of galactose (36.5%), arabinose (31.7%), and glucose (15.9%). Treating high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice with BTP prevented weight gain, lowered adiposity and reduced liver steatosis. title: Ligilactobacillus salivarius inhibits GII.4[P16] human norovirus replication in zebrafish larvae.
abstract: Human gut bacteria can modulate human norovirus (HuNoV) infection, underscoring the need to characterize virus-bacterium interactions. This study evaluated the effect of Ligilactobacillus salivarius on HuNoV GII.4[P16] replication using a zebrafish larva model. A GII.4[P16]-positive stool specimen was resuspended in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), centrifuged, and the supernatant stored at -80°C. title: Time-restricted feeding prevents acute liver injury by suppressing microbial anabolism of uric acid.
abstract: Time-restricted feeding (TRF) is known to improve metabolic and physiological rhythms; however, its role in acute liver injury (ALI) is unknown. Herein, we demonstrate that TRF ameliorates ALI through the gut microbiota across multiple murine models, particularly the acetaminophen-induced ALI. Specifically, TRF reduces host-derived 3-methylhistamine to decrease Prevotella intermedia (P. intermedia), which expresses adenosine deaminase (ADA) to generate uric acid (UA) in the gut. title: Dietary butyric acid modulates physiological, gut microbiota and transcriptomic responses of Penaeus vannamei under low salinity conditions.
abstract: Low salinity culture is increasingly adopted in the farming of Penaeus vannamei; however, nutritional strategies that specifically target physiological resilience and their underlying mechanisms under low salinity conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study evaluated the effects of dietary butyric acid supplementation (0%, 1%, 2%, and 4%) on growth performance, physiological responses, gut microbiota composition, and hepatopancreas transcriptome of juvenile P. vannamei reared at a sa
journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics

title: Propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, is associated with disease activity in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites found in fermented foods and produced by colonic bacterial fermentation of dietary fibers, may mediate gut-brain axis crosstalk influencing the course of multiple sclerosis (MS). In this study, SCFAs are measured in plasma and paired stool samples by targeted mass spectrometry in a large cohort of deeply phenotyped individuals shortly after MS onset. title: Gut microbiota-associated metabolic alterations contribute to 6PPD-Q-induced intestinal barrier dysfunction in mice.
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q), a ubiquitous tire-derived contaminant detected in environmental matrices and human samples, poses potential intestinal health risks to mammals. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. C57BL/6 mice were orally exposed to 6PPD-Q (4 mg/kg, once every 3 days for 28 days) with or without broad-spectrum antibiotic pretreatment to deplete gut microbiota. 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, immunofluoresc

title: Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid preserves dorsal hippocampal catecholamines to prevent post-stroke cognitive impairment.
abstract: Gut dysbiosis has been increasingly implicated in post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI); however, the causal contribution and therapeutic potential of gut microbiota-derived metabolites remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key microbiota-derived metabolites involved in PSCI and elucidate their underlying mechanisms. We found that both PSCI patients and middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice exhibited distinct gut microbial alterations, characterized by a marked reduction in trypt

title: Analysis of metabolic interactions in an artificial consortium including butyrogenic gut microbes.
abstract: Cross-feeding interactions shape gut microbial communities and contribute to the establishment of bacteria associated with beneficial fermentation products such as butyrate. However, many gut microbes involved in fiber degradation and butyrate-associated trophic networks remain poorly characterized. Here, we combined genomic analysis of candidate strains, genome-scale metabolic modeling, in vitro cultivation, and transcriptomics to investigate metabolic interactions among gut bacteria during gro

title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites.
abstract: Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort (n = 1,069: TwinsUK). title: A metabolite-centered framework for microbiota-gut-brain communication linking constrained signaling to behavior and stress physiology.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis links gut microbial activity with host neurophysiology and behavior, but its mechanistic interpretation remains fragmented across individual metabolites, biological compartments, and experimental systems. title: Microbiota-gut-brain axis dysregulation in irritable bowel syndrome: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and therapeutic implications. a narrative review.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a heterogeneous disorder of gut-brain interaction in which altered visceral sensitivity, motility, immune activity, epithelial permeability, and microbial metabolism may interact. Microbiota-related associations are frequently reported, but their direction and causal relevance remain uncertain. This narrative review critically examines clinical and mechanistic evidence concerning microbiota-gut-brain communication in IBS, including short-chain fatty acids, bile

title: Metabolic disease engineers the colorectal cancer ecosystem.
abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. title: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors.
abstract: Pediatric cholestatic liver diseases, such as Alagille syndrome and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, are rare genetic disorders characterized by impaired bile flow, systemic bile acid accumulation, and debilitating pruritus. Historically managed with supportive care or invasive surgical interventions, the therapeutic landscape has recently expanded with the introduction of ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitors. These luminal, ileum-targeted agents block bile acid reabsorpti
journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

title: EXPRESS: Dysbiosis correlates with more severe changes in intestinal function in cats with chronic enteropathy.
abstract: BackgroundMultiple pathophysiological mechanisms have been reported in animals with chronic enteropathy, as reflected by altered serum and fecal metabolites indicative of mucosal damage (e.g., fecal cholesterol, nervonic acid, arachidonic acid), malabsorption (e.g., serum cobalamin, fecal glucose), and loss of microbial function (e.g., fecal bile acid conversion). title: Non-redundant cardiolipin synthase family proteins shape lipid composition and stress resilience in Bacteroides fragilis.
abstract: Gut-resident bacteria must withstand membrane-disrupting stresses, such as bile acids, to persist in the intestinal environment. The Bacteroidota are a dominant phylum of the human gut microbiota. However, the genes responsible for the synthesis of membrane lipids in this phylum remain relatively uncharacterized. title: Microbiota-dependent citrulline metabolism alleviates sepsis by activating the aryl hydrocarbon receptor/IL-22 pathway to restore intestinal homeostasis.
abstract: This study investigated whether citrulline ameliorates sepsis-associated immune inflammation and intestinal barrier injury by modulating gut microbiota metabolites. Using an in vitro co-culture system and a cecal ligation and puncture mouse model, we found that citrulline fermentation products significantly increased the production of short-chain fatty acids and indole derivatives. title: Development and behavior of Steinernema hermaphroditum nematodes are impacted by a bacterial flavin monooxygenase.
abstract: Beneficial animal-microbe symbioses occur across the tree of life, with observable impacts on animal development and behavior. The bacterial enzyme complex HpaBC hydroxylates aromatic compounds, which may effect host neurotransmitter-dependent phenotypes. The bacterium Xenorhabdus griffiniae, a beneficial intestinal symbiont of Steinernema hermaphroditum entomopathogenic nematodes, encodes HpaBC. title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
abstract: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H2S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Podophyllotoxin-induced mammary gland injury via the gut-mammary gland axis mediated by gut microbiota-derived metabolite PAG and aberrant EGFR signaling in SD rats based on the toxicological evidence chain (TEC) concept.
abstract: Podophyllotoxin is a lignan isolated from Dysosma versipellis with well-established antitumor activity. In this study, we applied an upgraded toxicological evidence chain 2.0 framework to characterize podophyllotoxin-induced mammary toxicity in female rats and to probe the distal regulatory mechanism operating through the gut-mammary axis. title: Characterisation of Limosilactobacillus reuteri BG-R33®, an evolved aerotolerant derivative of the probiotic strain ATCC PTA 5289.
abstract: Probiotic strains intended for use in the oral cavity and upper respiratory tract are exposed to substantially higher oxygen levels than strains targeting the intestinal environment. We hypothesised that continuous oxygen exposure of an established probiotic strain used under conditions of high oxidative pressure, namely Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC PTA 5289 (Lr5289), would enable the natural selection of a variant better adapted to such an environment. title: Comparative transcriptional network analysis reveals ecological specialization in infant-associated species of Bifidobacterium.
abstract: Bifidobacterium species are important microorganisms in the infant gut microbiota displaying substantial genomic diversity, yet how this variability is reflected in transcriptional regulatory architecture remains an open question. title: Application of IgA-Seq in schizophrenia to identify key gut bacteria that promote abnormal behavior in mice.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) has a complex etiology, and growing evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Because abundance-based profiling does not identify taxa closely engaged by mucosal immunity, we used immunoglobulin A (IgA)-based bacterial sorting to prioritize candidate SCZ-associated gut bacteria and evaluated cultured consortia in mouse models. title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. title: Processing-controlled conjugation level of black tea polysaccharides regulates distinct microbial-metabolic pathways in intestinal protection.
abstract: Tea polysaccharides (TPS) usually conjugate with phenolics and proteins, but how conjugation levels affect their functionality is unclear. Here, black tea polysaccharides (BTPS) with graded conjugation levels were prepared by modulating enzymatic oxidation during rolling. Higher conjugation alters BTPS monosaccharide composition, particle size, surface charge, and morphology. title: Species-specific bacteriophage-mediated engineering of an artificial microbiome composed of Bacteroides and Phocaeicola species.
abstract: Members of the Bacteroides and Phocaeicola genera have been involved in various health- and disease-related states, but their in situ functions have not been clearly elucidated yet. Targeted removal of specific bacterial species using bacteriophages is expected to facilitate in situ functional analysis of gut bacteria. title: Multi-Omics Gut Microbiome Species Communities and Functional Modules Linking Metal Exposures to Children's Neurodevelopmental Health in a Canadian Birth Cohort.
abstract: Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. title: Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids control cGVHD development by regulating antibody production.
abstract: Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Microbe-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) exert diverse local effects on the intestinal mucosa. title: Impact of dietary exogenous carbohydrases in combination with sodium butyrate on growth performance, digestive tract health, and welfare aspects of broiler chickens fed with corn or wheat-based diets.
abstract: Exogenous enzymes and sodium butyrate supplementation may effectively alleviate the adverse effects of cereal non starch polysaccharides in broiler diets. title: Galactooligosaccharides reshape mucin O-glycosylation and gut microbial metabolism in DSS-challenged piglets.
abstract: The present study examined the effects of dietary galactooligosaccharides (GOS), a food-derived prebiotic carbohydrate, on colonic mucin O-glycosylation and gut microbiota in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-challenged weaned piglets. GOS supplementation reduced diarrhea incidence and colonic mucosal damage while enriching commensal taxa and increasing propionate and butyrate concentrations. title: Pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes gut microbial metabolic potential and alleviates estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss.
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a bone disease characterized by estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss. Although the gut microbiota has emerged as an important regulator of skeletal homeostasis, it remains unclear whether therapeutic benefits require preservation of the original microbial community. title: Microbial bile acid deconjugation counters metabolic decline in aging.
abstract: Interventions such as caloric restriction and time-restricted feeding improve lifespan and aging-associated metabolic health, in part through effects on the gut microbiome and bile acid dynamics. However, how aging alters microbial function and bile acid signaling, and whether these changes can be therapeutically leveraged, remain unclear. title: Engineering Microencapsulated Probiotics for Enhanced Aflatoxin M1 Mitigation in Milk.
abstract: Aflatoxin M1 is a major mycotoxin found primarily in milk and dairy products that causes a severe public health risk to dairy product safety and the dairy industry. Therefore, the present study explored the effectiveness of micro-encapsulated Lactobacillus acidophilus, Lactobacillus Casei and Bifidobacterium bifidum in reducing AFM1 in milk as promising and emerging strategies for eliminating and controlling AFM1 in milk. title: Schaftoside, a functional flavonoid from fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.), alleviates depression and cognitive deficits via the microbiome-gut-brain axis in stressed mice.
abstract: Depression involves dysregulation of central and peripheral networks, with gut microbiota alterations increasingly implicated in pathogenesis. Trigonella foenum-graecum L. (fenugreek), a functional food and medicinal herb, has been used traditionally for neurological disorders, yet its specific neuroprotective constituents remain poorly characterized. title: Gelatinization differentially impacts in vitro fermentation of high-amylose maize starch.
abstract: Some of the starch in a meal, depending on how it was thermally processed, may escape complete digestion in the upper gut and pass into the colon as available for microbial fermentation. This study uses an in vitro batch fecal model to examine the fermentability of high-amylose maize starch (HAMS) that has been gelatinized to different degrees (DG). title: Prebiotic effects of lotus seed starch-C18 fatty acid complexes: Role of structural changes during in vitro digestion and fermentation.
abstract: Despite growing interest in starch-lipid complexes as prebiotic ingredients, the impact of fatty acid (FA) unsaturation on their fermentative behavior and gut microbiota modulation remains controversial, largely due to inconsistent structural characterization across studies. Herein, lotus seed starch (LS), notable for its high amylose content, was used to systematically fabricate complexes with C18 FAs of varying unsaturation, such as stearic (SA), oleic (OA), linoleic (LA), and α-linolenic (ALA

title: Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid suppresses osteoclast formation by promoting IL-10+ Breg differentiation via AhR signaling.
abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites play pivotal roles in immune and bone homeostasis; however, the specific metabolites involved in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the role of indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a microbial metabolite of tryptophan, in estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss through integrated microbiome, metabolomic, and immunological analyses. title: Akkermansia muciniphila alleviates osteoporosis by suppressing bone marrow adiposity through the gut microbiota-UDCA-TGR5 axis.
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is characterized not only by progressive bone loss but also frequently by pathological bone marrow adiposity (BMA) expansion. Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK), implicated in lipid metabolic homeostasis, was previously found to be markedly depleted during estrogen deficiency-associated bone loss. title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA-AhR-GLP-1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)-AhR-GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching Ligilactobacillus. title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. title: Sodium L-lactate alleviates DSS-induced colitis through gut microbiota remodeling and Akkermansia enrichment.
abstract: L-lactate, a byproduct of glycolysis and hypoxia, accumulates in the gut during disease progression and may affect host responses and microbial metabolism. Here, we investigated the protective effect of sodium L-lactate on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice and the involvement of the gut microbiota. title: In vivo pharmacokinetics and lactic acidosis toxicity of Phenformin mediated by gut microbiota in control and pseudo-germ-free rats.
abstract: Phenformin, a classic biguanide, was withdrawn clinically due to severe lactic acidosis, while the non-genetic causes of interindividual toxic susceptibility remain elusive. This study aimed to clarify pharmacokinetics and lactic acidosis toxicity of phenformin mediated by gut microbiota.

title: Prenatal Bifidobacterium bifidum intervention alleviates early-life stress-induced neurobehavioral abnormalities via inhibiting neuroinflammation in offspring mice.
abstract: Early-life stress is a key environmental risk factor for neurobehavioral abnormalities in offspring, which disrupts gut-brain axis homeostasis and causes neurodevelopmental damage. Probiotics have shown important potential in improving neurodevelopmental abnormalities. As a dominant gut microbe in healthy mother-infant pairs, Bifidobacterium bifidum is closely related to neurobehavioral abnormalities. title: Identification and characterization of polysaccharide from Paeoniae Radix Rubra, and its mechanism in alleviating anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury based on integrating gut microbiota and non-targeted metabolomics.
abstract: A novel polysaccharide, designated PRRP2, was extracted from the dried root of Paeoniae Radix Rubra. Structural analysis suggested that the PRRP2 backbone was predominantly composed of →4)-Glcp-(1→ and →6)-Glcp-(1→ glycosidic linkages, with a trace amount of →2)-Xylp-(1→ embedded within the backbone. journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis

title: Changes in the Cecal Microbiota in a Rat Model of Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease.
abstract: Characteristics of the intestinal microbiota specific to metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) were studied in vivo using male Wistar rats. The consumption of high-fat diets (choline-deficient or cholesterol-supplemented) commonly used in experimental MAFLD models induced shifts in the cecal microbiota. title: Dietary Clostridium butyricum NCU-02 and Its Postbiotic Butyrate Ameliorate Autism Spectrum Disorder-like Symptoms: Involvement of Hippocampal Oxidative Stress Modulation.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition closely linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, yet effective dietary interventions remain limited. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum NCU-02, a probiotic candidate, and its sterile supernatant in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced mouse model of ASD, with emphasis on their postbiotic properties. Both treatments significantly ameliorated core ASD-like behaviors, attenuating

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder.
abstract: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. Using aged laying hens, a livestock model with a relatively short digestive tract, we examined the gut microbiota, faecal metabolome, and breast-muscle metabolome by integrative multi-omics analyses in hens fed a Caldifermentibacillus hisashii-containing fermented feed or a control diet. title: Late-life depletion of the gut microbiome attenuates aging-induced frailty in male mice.
abstract: Frailty summarizes aging-related decline independently of chronological age. Although the gut microbiome covaries with frailty in older populations, its causal contribution to frailty remains unclear. We profiled middle-aged (72-week-old) and young (10-week-old) male mice across six data layers including physio-behavioral phenotypes, fecal metagenomic taxa and pathways, serum lipidome, and liver and hippocampal transcriptomes. title: Effects of succinate supplementation on rumen fermentation, microbiota, and propionate-associated metabolism in vitro
abstract: Introduction Succinate is an intermediate in the ruminal succinate-propionate pathway, but its direct effects as an exogenous additive on rumen fermentation, bacterial community structure, and energy-related metabolites remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated whether graded succinate supplementation changes in vitro rumen fermentation and propionate-associated microbial and metabolite profiles. title: Muribaculum intestinale restricts Salmonella Typhimurium colonization by converting succinate to propionate
abstract: Abstract Insufficient dietary fiber intake is associated with dysbiosis and compromised colonization resistance (CR) to enteric infections. However, a detailed understanding of the relationship between dietary fiber insufficiency and CR remains elusive. Our study aimed to delineate the impact of fiber deprivation on gut microbiome and CR in a murine model with Salmonella Typhimurium infection. title: Gut-resident Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens decreases fat accumulation via MYC-driven epigenetic regulation of arginine biosynthesis
abstract: Uncovering the mechanisms of excessive fat accumulation in livestock can not only protect animal health but also maintain the revenue of the intensive feeding industry. In this study, a bacteria-wide association study was conducted in a cohort of 129 commercial Yorkshire pigs. We found that Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens (P. succinatutens) was a key bacterium with greater abundance in low backfat thickness (LBF) pigs and was positively correlated with serum arginine concentrations. title: Human gut microbiota and their production of endocannabinoid-like mediators are directly affected by a dietary oil
abstract: ABSTRACT Dietary omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) and the gut microbiome affect each other. We investigated the impact of supplementation with Buglossoides arvensis oil (BO), rich in stearidonic acid (SDA), on the human gut microbiome. Employing the Mucosal Simulator of the Human Intestinal Microbial Ecosystem (M-SHIME), we simulated the ileal and ascending colon microbiomes of four donors. title: Microbiome-derived bile acids contribute to elevated antigenic response and bone erosion in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. It has been widely recognized that gut microbial dysbiosis is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of RA, although distinct alterations in microbiota have been associated with this disease. Yet, the metabolites that mediate the impacts of the gut microbiome on RA are less well understood. title: Growth of succinate consumer Dialister hominis is supported by Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron.
abstract: This study revealed an interaction between the gut commensal bacterium Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron JCM 5827T and asaccharolytic bacterium Dialister hominis JCM 33369T, which uses succinate instead of carbohydrates for growth. D. hominis usually forms extremely small colonies on Brucella blood agar plates. title: Microbial interaction between the succinate‐utilizing bacterium Phascolarctobacterium faecium and the gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
abstract: A large variety of microbes are present in the human gut, some of which are considered to interact with each other. Most of these interactions involve bacterial metabolites. Phascolarctobacterium faecium hardly uses carbohydrates for growth and instead uses succinate as a substrate. This study investigated the growth behavior of the co‐culture of the succinate‐specific utilizer P. faecium and the succinogenic gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron. The virome of New Zealand fur seals reveals novel viral diversity and evidence of continued Canine distemper virus circulation
abstract: Canine distemper virus (CDV) has recently been detected in New Zealand fur seals (Arctocephalus forsteri), including retrospective samples from 2020 and outbreaks associated with substantial mortality in late 2024 and 2025. However, the geographic distribution of CDV and the broader viral diversity harboured by New Zealand fur seals remain poorly understood. title: Not all plant-based diets are alike: intake of minimally processed plant foods is associated with gut microbial richness among vegetarians and vegans.
abstract: Plant-based diets are usually defined by what they exclude, overlooking which plant foods are eaten and how processed they are. Here we examine whether this overlooked dimension is related to the gut microbiome. In a cross-sectional study of 172 omnivorous, lacto-ovo-vegetarian and vegan adults profiled by shotgun metagenomics, vegetarians and vegans harboured fewer gut species than omnivores. title: Comparative exometabolome and extracellular-vesicle metabolome of Bifidobacterium
abstract: Bifidobacterium species are early colonisers of the human gut and are widely used as probiotics, yet their extracellular chemistry remains largely unexplored, and the small-molecule cargo of their extracellular vesicles (EVs) has not been characterised. title: EFFECT OF A LACTOBACILLUS POSTBIOTIC ON DIGESTIVE HEALTH IN DOGS RAISED IN CONDITIONS AT RISK OF GIARDIA DUODENALIS INFECTION
abstract: Giardia duodenalis infection is associated with diarrhea and dysbiosis in dogs, while metronidazole treatment can further disrupt the microbiota. We evaluated adjunctive LB fermentate HF (LBHF), a Lactobacillus-derived postbiotic, in a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study of 30 naturally infected dogs (Terriers).
